title: Shared secret mismatch — packet rejected before authentication
plain_english: The server received the request but threw it away before looking at any credentials: the Message-Authenticator check failed, which almost always means the shared secret configured on your NAS (switch, AP, controller) does not match the secret in this server's clients.conf. The user's password was never even evaluated, so no amount of credential fixing will help.

causes.cause: The shared secret on the NAS and in clients.conf genuinely differ — a typo, a stale value from a previous server, or trailing whitespace copied into one side.
causes.next_check: Re-type (don't paste) the secret on both the NAS and in clients.conf, then re-run radiusd -X and retest. Some NAS firmwares silently truncate secrets longer than 31 characters — try a shorter secret if in doubt.

causes.cause: The request matched a different client{} block than you think — overlapping subnets or a catch-all 0.0.0.0/0 entry carrying another secret.
causes.next_check: In the radiusd -X output, note the packet's source IP and confirm which client entry FreeRADIUS matched it to; look for broader client definitions that shadow the specific one.

causes.cause: NAT or a load balancer rewrites the packet's source IP, so it arrives under an address bound to the wrong client definition.
causes.next_check: Compare the source IP shown in the debug output with the NAS's real management IP; if they differ, add a client entry for the NAT address or fix the routing.
